summary.description: One or two sentences: what the requested change is, in your own words.

approach.description: How you would implement it and why, in a short paragraph.

files.description: Files you expect to create or change.

acceptanceCriteria.description: What must be true when the change is done, each specific enough to check, and how it is checked. From the acceptance criteria in the request, or proposed by you when it has none.

criterion.description: One observable outcome, for example: GET /tasks lists open overdue tasks first.

check.description: How it is checked: the test that will cover it, or the command or manual step when a test cannot.

testPlan.description: The tests the change adds or updates, across every test layer it touches (the test layers in the project CLAUDE.md, leaving out rows still marked Example; unit tests when it lists none). Empty only for a change with no behaviour, such as docs only.

id.description: Unique in the plan: the ID of the layer from the Test layers table (its initial when the table has no ID) and a number, for example D1, U2, J1.

layer.description: The test layer, as the project names it, for example Database or Journey (Unit when the project lists no layers).

proves.description: What the test proves: the input or state and the observable outcome.

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria it covers, by their number in acceptanceCriteria (1 is the first). Empty for a test the project rules require, or one that only replaces an old test.

replaces.description: An existing test the change makes wrong, which this test replaces or updates. Empty when none.

skippedLayers.description: Each test layer of the project with no test in testPlan, and why the change does not need one.

risks.description: What could go wrong or needs care (data, security, compatibility).

questions.description: Decisions only the requester can make. Empty when nothing is unclear.

readyToBuild.description: True only when there are no open questions and the plan can be built as written.
